parameters.note: RECOMMENDATION: HR green (HR2, 3057 /mm, 4730-5450 A) as the HR blue-arm setting.  Why: it holds the Mg b triplet and Fe lines of the Galactic archaeology HR survey (the largest HR program), Jin et al. 2024 describe GA-HR in the 'green+red HR mode' and run the simulated data in 'green+red'.  The 'blue' grating (HR1, 4040-4650 A) is offered as an optional fifth Setting.  The published wording lists red+green first and red+blue second ('the red+green or red+blue grating combination'); no source gives usage counts, so 'most used' is an INFERENCE from the surveys' science.

not_found: The Rogers et al. 2014 spectrograph design paper (SPIE 9147, "The design of the WEAVE spectrograph", ADS 2014SPIE.9147E..6HR): no open copy was reachable (SPIE refuses automated access; no arXiv version). Its role is covered by Dalton et al. 2014 Sec. 6, the INAF/NOVA papers and the ING pages.

The collimator-correction lens prescriptions, the camera lens prescriptions and the camera focal length in mm (f/1.8 on 190 mm gives 342 mm, DERIVED; the dispersions confirm it to 1-2 percent for three of five gratings).
The dichroic transition width and its measured transmission curve.
A measured R(lambda) from arc lines: the resolving powers published are nominal, and the 2025 as-built shortfall of the blue arm is stated without numbers (ING).
Collimator-to-dichroic, dichroic-to-VPH, VPH-to-camera distances as numbers in a text or table: all are MEASURED from the Zemax-type layout (INGF), +/- 4-6 percent.
The gap in the MOS slit between slitlets in microns (published as 'about one fiber').
The optical-bench lens spacings in HR mode (the figure ING_vhires.gif shows the camera swung to the HR position).
The VPH fringe slant angle and film thickness in numbers (BIA: fringes 'slanted'; substrate thickness 38 and 50 mm only; efficiency curves are plots).

conflicts.topic: Focal ratio at the prime focus
conflicts.text: f/2.75 (MIG, SAY: design), 2.8 on axis and 2.9 at 1 deg radius (INGLP, as built). The explorer needs only the f/3.1-3.2 fiber-side values.

conflicts.topic: Collimator described as 'reflective' (DAL 2014) and 'off-axis catadioptric' (JIN 2024) and 'a spherical collimator mirror' (IZA 2018)
conflicts.text: These are consistent: a spherical mirror plus corrector lenses (spherical surfaces) placed after the dichroic in each arm. The explorer draws a mirror collimator.

IZA (INAOE, the polisher): 660 mm diameter, 624 mm clear aperture, OHARA CLEARCERAM-Z HS, radius 1224.65 mm.  INGLP: 'Size 645 mm x 260 mm, material Zerodur'. Possibly a later cut-down of the blank (not stated); the 660 mm round blank with a 624 mm clear aperture is the polisher's own statement.

INGLP: 'Littrow mode ... equal: 20 deg in low-res mode, and 51.6 deg in high-res mode'.  BIA Table 1: blue LR 22.72 / 17.01 deg, blue HR1 54.43 / 48.98, blue HR2 54.46 / 48.98, red LR 19.82 / 19.86, red HR 51.59 / 51.65 deg (the Bragg condition is not matched: slanted fringes).  The red gratings agree with ING (51.6); the blue ones do not.  The preset follows BIA (the grating design document); psi = alpha + beta.

ING scale 0.076 (HR1) and 0.090 (HR2) A/px; the BIA angles with f_cam = 342 mm give 0.0804 and 0.0942 (5.8 and 4.6 percent higher).  Using beta = 51.6 deg (the INGLP 'equal angles') instead would give 0.0761 and 0.0891, matching ING.  The 2025 realignment (ING page) and the 'expected' values may explain it; unresolved.
5900 A (ING, INGLP) vs 600 nm (DAL 2014); the LR bands overlap 5790-6060 A (JIN Table 3), centered 5925 A. The preset uses 5900 A.

MIG: fibers deliver f/3.1; SAY: spectrograph f/3.1 and FRD loss 11 percent outside f/3.1 (prototype); but SAY's test-bench requirement RTS 01 reads 'Output aperture F/2.7 +/- 0.2'. Read here as a test requirement for the output cone, not the spectrograph acceptance; INFERRED.
Nominal 20,000 (ING, JIN) vs the geometric full width of the fiber image: 16,550 (blue HR) and 17,510 (red HR), DERIVED.  The LR values agree (4919 and 5001 against 5000).
ING (13 Mar 2026): surveys expected to begin about mid-2026; SPIE 2026 abstract (Aug 2026): 'expected to be in full science operations in early 2027'.
